claims.text: Accelerated coupled degradation in the multi-phase eutectic HEA is driven by synergy between mechanically induced surface deformation and thermally activated intergranular corrosion.
Intergranular corrosion weakens phase boundaries and thereby promotes material removal.
The initial alloy has distinct phase boundaries.
The alloy microstructure is stable at room temperature.
The proposed intervention is simultaneous mechanical sliding or abrasion and corrosive exposure at elevated temperature.
The relevant elevated-temperature condition is above 300°C.
Acidic or oxidizing media provide the relevant corrosive environment.
Phase boundaries and intergranular regions are the structural mediator of coupled degradation.
Elevated temperature activates preferential corrosion of intergranular regions and phase boundaries.
Preferential corrosion reduces the mechanical integrity of intergranular regions and phase boundaries.
Mechanical wear deforms the surface and exposes fresh surfaces.
Freshly exposed surfaces are more susceptible to subsequent corrosion.
The feedback between wear-induced exposure and corrosion accelerates material removal relative to either process acting alone.
The simultaneous-exposure degradation rate will be significantly greater than the sum of separately measured wear-only and corrosion-only rates.
Wear will increase during simultaneous exposure because corrosion weakens phase boundaries.
Corrosion will increase during simultaneous exposure because wear exposes fresh reactive surfaces.
The comparison uses wear-only and corrosion-only degradation rates measured at the same temperature and otherwise matched environmental settings.
The hypothesis applies when both wear and corrosion are active and temperature is sufficient to activate intergranular corrosion.
Wear-only, corrosion-only, and simultaneous-exposure tests at the same elevated temperature can distinguish synergistic degradation from additive degradation.
Failure to observe super-additive total degradation or preferential intergranular corrosion and phase-boundary weakening would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The conditions specify above 300°C as the relevant range, while the uncertainty field states that the temperature threshold for significant intergranular corrosion is unknown.
